record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: For each left-Σ^0_2 real r in [0,1], there is a computable profinite group together with a computable subgroup of Hausdorff dimension r. Which values of r can still occur if the ambient profinite group G is additionally required to be topologically finitely generated?

evidence.quote: For each left Σ2 real r ∈ [0, 1] there is a computable profinite group and computable subgroup with Hausdorff dimension r. Problem 16. Which values can occur for r when G is also topologically finitely generated?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $G$ be a profinite group, equipped with its inverse-limit topology and a fixed descending filtration $G = G_0 \supseteq G_1 \supseteq G_2 \supseteq \cdots$ of open normal subgroups with $\bigcap_n G_n = \{1\}$. The Hausdorff dimension of a closed subgroup $H \le G$ (with respect to this filtration) is
$$\dim_H(H) \;=\; \liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log [H G_n : G_n]}{\log [G : G_n]} \;\in\; [0,1].$$

A profinite group $G$ is called computable if it is presented as the inverse limit of a computable sequence of finite groups $G/G_n$ together with computable transition maps; a closed subgroup $H \le G$ is computable if the sequence of finite images $HG_n/G_n \le G/G_n$ is uniformly computable. The group $G$ is topologically finitely generated if there exist finitely many elements whose generated subgroup is dense in $G$.

A real number $r \in [0,1]$ is called left-$\Sigma^0_2$ if the set of rationals $\{q \in \mathbb{Q} : q < r\}$ is $\Sigma^0_2$ in the arithmetical hierarchy (equivalently, $r$ is the supremum of a computable sequence of $\Delta^0_2$ rationals).

Known fact. For every left-$\Sigma^0_2$ real $r \in [0,1]$, there exist a computable profinite group $G$ and a computable closed subgroup $H \le G$ with $\dim_H(H) = r$.

Problem. Characterize the set of those $r \in [0,1]$ that arise as $\dim_H(H)$ for some computable closed subgroup $H$ of some computable profinite group $G$ which is, in addition, topologically finitely generated.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any published resolution. The question is listed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory, and related literature on Hausdorff spectra of topologically finitely generated profinite groups (e.g., recent work on finitely generated Hausdorff spectra and on regular branch groups) addresses general structural questions but does not characterize which left-$\Sigma^0_2$ reals are realizable in the topologically finitely generated computable setting.

status_evidence.title: On finitely generated Hausdorff spectra of groups acting on rooted trees
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the finitely generated Hausdorff spectrum of a profinite group has proven to be in general a difficult problem... not many examples in the literature where the finitely generated Hausdorff spectrum of a group has been computed.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art on finitely generated Hausdorff spectra is limited, consistent with the problem being open.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm to compute the Hausdorff dimension of regular branch groups
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit algorithm for Hausdorff dimension of generalized regular branch profinite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic results exist for special classes but do not address the general computability characterization.

status_evidence.title: Hausdorff dimension of closed subsets in profinite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Hausdorff dimensions of closed subsets/subgroups in profinite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Background literature does not characterize the realizable values for topologically finitely generated computable profinite groups.
